sections.title: Basic Concept of Paper Folding
sections.content: In paper folding questions, a square or rectangular sheet is folded one or more times and then a cut or hole is made. When the paper is unfolded, the cut appears on all the folded layers. The key idea is that each fold increases the number of layers.

sections.title: Half and Quarter Folding
sections.content: If a paper is folded once (horizontally or vertically), it forms 2 layers. If it is folded again, it forms 4 layers. For example, one horizontal and one vertical fold divide the paper into four equal parts.

sections.title: Hole at the Center
sections.content: If a circular hole is punched at the center of the folded paper, it will appear on every layer when unfolded. For 2 folds (4 layers), one hole becomes 4 identical holes placed symmetrically.

sections.title: Corner Cut
sections.content: If a small square or triangle is cut from the folded corner, the same cut will appear on all corresponding corners after unfolding. In a quarter fold (4 layers), one corner cut results in 4 similar corner cuts.

sections.title: Semicircle Cut on the Edge
sections.content: If a semicircle is cut along the folded edge, unfolding may form a full circle. The final shape depends on the direction of the fold.

sections.title: 3-Step Solution Method
sections.content: Step 1: Count the number of folds. Step 2: Determine the number of layers (1 fold = 2 layers, 2 folds = 4 layers). Step 3: Identify the position of the cut (center, edge, or corner) and imagine how it will repeat symmetrically.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Miscounting the number of layers. 2. Ignoring symmetry. 3. Forgetting that each layer gets the same cut. 4. Choosing an option without checking the total number of shapes formed.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: To solve paper folding questions, count the folds, calculate the layers, and apply symmetry. The number of final shapes usually equals the number of layers when the cut passes through all layers.

tricks.title: Layer Doubling Rule
tricks.explanation: Each fold doubles the number of layers.
tricks.example: 2 folds = 4 layers, so 1 hole becomes 4 holes.

tricks.title: Center Cut Rule
tricks.explanation: A cut at the exact center spreads evenly in all directions.
tricks.example: After 2 folds, one center hole forms 4 identical center holes.

tricks.title: Corner Cut Rule
tricks.explanation: A cut at a folded corner appears on all matching corners after unfolding.
tricks.example: Quarter fold + 1 corner cut = 4 corner cuts.

tricks.title: Edge Semicircle Trick
tricks.explanation: A semicircle cut on a folded edge may become a full circle when opened.
tricks.example: Semicircle on fold line → full circle after unfolding.

tricks.title: Symmetry Check
tricks.explanation: The final design will always be symmetrical along the fold lines.
tricks.example: If the cut is on the right side, a mirror cut appears on the left.

tricks.title: Visualize All Layers Together
tricks.explanation: Imagine that all folded layers are stacked and cut at once.
tricks.example: A small square cut on folded paper appears on every layer.

tricks.title: Eliminate by Count
tricks.explanation: Remove options where the number of shapes does not match the number of layers.
tricks.example: If there are 4 layers, an option showing 3 holes is incorrect.

tricks.title: Follow the 3-Step Rule
tricks.explanation: Count folds → Count layers → Apply symmetry.
